walkthroughs.body_html:
Kinematics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Kinematics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Kinematics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²

mcqs.q: What must you remember to include when finding an indefinite integral?
options: You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
You don't need anything extra — the integral is just the antiderivative.
Add the two equations together and solve as if it were a single equation.
A constant of integration (+ C), because the derivative of any constant is zero.

mcqs.q: What does it mean to solve a pair of simultaneous equations?
options: You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
Add the two equations together and solve as if it were a single equation.
Solve each equation separately and write both sets of answers.
Find the values of the variables that satisfy both equations at the same time (the point where the two lines meet).
14, because you read and calculate left to right (3 + 4 = 7, then 7 x 2).
11 — multiplication is done before addition (3 + 8 = 11).
9, because you add all the numbers and then subtract the operator count.
You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vertical motion under gravity”?
options: Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “SUVAT equations”?
options: If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
